newsitem.title: USA: US spot jet diffs swell, offsetting NYMEX decline.
newsitem.headline: US spot jet diffs swell, offsetting NYMEX decline.

text.p: U.S. spot jet fuel prices rose about a half cent Tuesday as differentials expanded one cent a gallon in both centers on refiner buying, more than offsetting a moderate decline in February heating oil futures.
Traders said Gulf Coast distillates were helped by numerous early maintenance turnarounds on Refinery Row and a recent cutback on distillate production in favor of gasoline output.
"Refineries have been putting distillates on the back burner, so supplies have tightened up" in recent days, one Gulf player said.
"It's gotten pretty darned strong pretty darned fast," another Gulf trader said, with aviation-quality 54-grade offered at 0.25 cent over the February print.
Traders said several majors remain in the market, adding that British Petroleum and Mobil had been active last week and that numerous Gulf jet fuel cargoes are headed or destined for the West Coast.

New York 54-grade, meanwhile, saw diffs firm to between 4.0 and 4.50 cents above the print. "They're not moving enough jet up the Colonial Pipeline," one East Coast player said, noting the pipeline is on allocation through February.
